The  concept  of  motivation  focuses  on  explaining  what  moves behaviour.  In  fact,  the  term  (625)  ________is  derived  from  the Latin  word  'movere,  referring  to  movement  of  activity.  Most of our  everyday  explanation  of  (626)_______  is  given  in  terms  of motives. Motives also help in making (627)_______about behaviour.  A  person  will  work  hard  in  school,  in  sports,  in business, in music, and in many other situations, if he/she has a very strong need for (628)_______Hence, motives are the general states  that  enable  us  to  make  predictions  about  behaviour  in many different  situations.  In  other  words,  motivation  is  one of the (629)_______of behaviour. Instincts, drives, needs, goals, and incentives come under the broad cluster of motivation.
- Q.625. (a) human behaviour                 (b) instinct
- (c) motivation                             (d) psychology
- Q.626.
- (a) behavior    (b) motivation       (c) goal     (d) incentive

Fingerprinting  is  the  one  of  the  methods of (630)_______ using the  impression made by the minute ridge formation or patterns found  on the fingertips. No two persons have exactly the same (631)_______ of ridge patterns, they remain unchanged throughout  the  life.  Fingerprints may be classified and filled on the basis  of  the  ridge  patterns,  setting  up  an  identification system  that  is  almost  (632)_______.  Today,  law  enforcement agencies use computers to (633)_______ record fingerprints and to transmit them electronically to other agencies for comparison. By comparing fingerprints of the criminals with the recorded  fingerprints,  officials  can  establish (634)_______ proof of the presence or identity of a person.
- Q.630. (a) involvement
- (b) satisfaction
- (c) demonstration
- (d) identification
- Q.631. (a) arrangement
- (b) statement
- (c) management
- (d) settlement
- Q.632.
- (a) risky          (b) infallible   (c) unreliable       (d) fallible
